item.title: Harnessing multi-source geospatial big data to construct a pan-Arctic building footprint atlas: integrating geometric, morphological, temporal, and functional attributes
item.dc:title: Harnessing multi-source geospatial big data to construct a pan-Arctic building footprint atlas: integrating geometric, morphological, temporal, and functional attributes
item.dc:creator: Shimeng Zhao Jiayi Wang Xiao Cheng Yize Guo Qi Zhang Peijie Wang Weijia Li Da He Chong Liu a School of Geospatial Engineering and Science, Sun Yat-sen University, Guangzhou, Chinab Ministry of Education, Key Laboratory of Comprehensive Observation of Polar Environment (Sun Yat-sen University), Zhuhai, Chinac Department of Geography and Environment, University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, Chapel Hill, USAd Shenzhen International Graduate School, Tsinghua University, Shenzhen, Chinae School of Geography and Planning, Sun Yat-sen University, Guangzhou, ChinaShimeng Zhao is an M.S. student at the School of Geospatial Engineering and Science, Sun Yat-sen University. Her research focuses on individual building footprint extraction from high-resolution remote sensing imagery and the development of high-resolution infrastructure datasets for Arctic and other challenging environments. Jiayi Wang is an M.S. student at the School of Geospatial Engineering and Science, Sun Yat-sen University. Her research focuses on mapping and interpretation of sparse human infrastructure in high-latitude environments. Xiao Cheng is a Professor at Sun Yat-sen University, where he serves as Dean of the School of Geospatial Engineering and Science, Director of the Polar Research Center, and Director of the Key Laboratory of Comprehensive Observation of Polar Environment, Ministry of Education. His research focuses on polar remote sensing, atmosphere-ice-ocean-land interactions, ice shelf and glacier dynamics, sea-ice parameter retrieval, and polar climate change. He received the Award for Advanced Individual of China’s Polar Exploration in 2017. Yize Guo is an M.S. student at the School of Geospatial Engineering and Science, Sun Yat-sen University. His research focuses on the remote sensing characterization of Arctic surface properties and environmental conditions. Qi Zhang is a Research Assistant Professor in the Department of Geography and Environment at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. His research focuses on coupled human and natural systems, land-use change, forest conservation, and household livelihoods. His work contributes to understanding the spatial processes linking land systems, infrastructure, and socio-ecological change. Peijie Wang is an M.S. student at the School of Geospatial Engineering and Science, Sun Yat-sen University. His research focuses on multimodal remote sensing and multi-source data fusion. Weijia Li is an Associate Professor at the Shenzhen International Graduate School, Tsinghua University. She received her bachelor’s degree from Sun Yat-sen University and her Ph.D. from Tsinghua University. Her research interests include computer vision, large multimodal models, and urban remote sensing, with a focus on extracting and interpreting built-environment information from multi-source geospatial data. Da He is an Associate Professor at the School of Geography and Planning, Sun Yat-sen University. His research interests include multi- and hyperspectral remote sensing image classification, deep learning, data fusion, and change detection. Chong Liu is an Associate Professor at the School of Geospatial Engineering and Science, Sun Yat-sen University. He received the B.S. degree in remote sensing science and technology and his Ph.D. degree in photogrammetry and remote sensing from Wuhan University in 2010 and 2015, respectively. His research focuses on satellite remote sensing, land-cover mapping and monitoring, Arctic and permafrost environments, and geospatial big data analytics.
